rubrics.criterion: Every seam on the cluster-connection path that received the connection data as a run of separate positional parameters now receives it as a cohesive grouped value: the Elasticsearch adapter's construction, the exported auth-header derivation helper, and the connection store's cluster-update action. A grouped value here means a real domain-shaped bearing (the address-bearing connection value, the auth value on its own, or another sound typed grouping of the same fields) — not a flat per-site bag in which every credential field is loosely typed and independent again.
rubrics.rationale: These three boundaries are the actual receive seams of the case; a repair that regroups only the most visible one (usually the adapter constructor) leaves two production seams still dissolving the data group.

rubrics.criterion: Every production feeding path passes the grouped value instead of enumerating fields: the connect-screen connection test, the connect-and-save flow, the lazily created request client for the active cluster, the periodic home-cluster health refresh, the standalone cluster-health helper, the REST-tab fetch path that derives its own authorization header, and the cluster-edit save path. No touched call site still passes three or more fields of one source record as separate arguments into these boundaries.
rubrics.rationale: The seven feeding sites are where the data group is physically dismantled; any unrepaired site keeps the per-field burden the task asks to remove and would silently reappear at the next signature change.

rubrics.criterion: The authentication mode information remains discriminated and typed after the repair: each auth mode still carries exactly the fields that mode uses (basic auth username/password, API key, AWS IAM key/secret/optional token/region, none with no credentials), through the existing mode-bearing value or an equivalent typed construction — the grouping does not dissolve the distinction between auth modes into one everything-optional shape.
rubrics.rationale: The case's central data group is mode-plus-credentials; a grouping that flattens the mode discrimination back into parallel optional fields reproduces the underlying weakness inside the new container.

rubrics.criterion: The grouping is consistent across the connection path rather than re-invented per site: boundaries that need the same data use the same shared value/type (the connection-bearing value where the address is needed, the auth value where it is not), including the store-update call which still reaches the persisted cluster list, and the header derivation called from both the adapter and the REST fetch path.
rubrics.rationale: The point of the transport rework is that one cluster-connection concept crosses the whole path; per-call-site improvised containers keep every future change a many-place edit.

rubrics.criterion: Saving an edited cluster still behaves as before end-to-end: the cluster-edit flow still merges the edited name, address and auth into the saved cluster at the right index, the same auth cleanup on save still runs, and the persisted representation of saved clusters (read by existing sessions and the migration code) is unchanged.
rubrics.rationale: The store seam was deliberately loosened to values plus an index selector; a repair that also reshapes the persisted cluster objects would silently break stored sessions, which the task's compatibility boundary forbids.

rubrics.criterion: The permissive per-site credential widenings introduced only to read individual fields (the inline 'anything-goes' property-bag locals holding username/password/apiKey/access-key material at each construction or header site, or equivalent replacements) do not survive the repair.
rubrics.rationale: Those casts exist solely to defeat the discriminated auth typing for the field-by-field handover; keeping them alongside a grouped transport is exactly the leftover plumbing the task asks to clean up.

rubrics.criterion: No dead per-field parameters or unused credential values remain at any touched boundary or in any grouping introduced by the repair (every field of the grouped values can still influence behavior somewhere on the connection path, and no signature keeps a parameter only for compatibility with the old flattened calls).
rubrics.rationale: The case was built so every flattened parameter was genuinely consumed; a repair that leaves unused members in its grouping trades one loose end for another.

rubrics.criterion: Runtime behavior per auth mode is unchanged: no Authorization header is attached for auth mode none; basic auth and API key produce byte-identical headers via the same tested helper; AWS IAM clusters still sign requests with the same key/secret/token/region/service values; and cluster addresses keep the same trailing-slash normalization so request URLs are byte-identical.
rubrics.rationale: These seams carry real transport behavior; grouping code may not alter which values reach the wire for any of the four modes.

rubrics.criterion: The shared request client is still created lazily against the currently active cluster on first use and pinged before the first request, and follows cluster selection: no eager construction at startup, no caching keyed to a stale cluster, and no leakage of one cluster's credentials into a request for another cluster after switching, adding or editing clusters.
rubrics.rationale: The data view path builds one client for whichever cluster is active; a repair that wires construction differently (or reuses a single client across clusters) regresses multi-cluster workflows that have no direct unit coverage.

rubrics.criterion: The unit-tested helper contracts on the connection path are untouched: basic header building, the URI/credential URL helper, cluster migration, predefined-cluster builders, and query/table builders keep their existing signatures and those suites pass unchanged.
rubrics.rationale: The task's preservation boundary explicitly pins these helpers; a repair that 'improves' them alongside the transport work would rewrite protected, unrelated behavior.

rubrics.criterion: The observable connect/test/health flows keep their state semantics: success, error and loading transitions and their incident messages still occur exactly on the same events, the periodic health refresh interval still runs over the saved clusters, and the connect flow still stores version, distribution, flavor, status and uuid exactly as before.
rubrics.rationale: These flows are the user-visible surface of the connection path; a regrouping that changes when state flips or which cluster metadata is stored would be a behavior change disguised as cleanup.
